claim: writeResources now writes OS-native file clipboard formats on ordinary internal local copies, so an in-app Ctrl+V also satisfies the explorer DOM paste listener's clipboardData.files guard, firing filesExplorer.paste a second time (double paste + spurious confirm dialog).
raw: **1. Writing the OS-native file clipboard format on ordinary *internal* copies re-triggers the native-paste path, causing a double paste and a spurious "confirm paste" dialog.**

claim: resolveClipboardResources replaces each vscode-remote:// source with a downloaded local temp file:// URI, so same-folder copy/paste in a remote workspace fails with "already exists" instead of auto-renaming.
raw: **2. Copy/paste into the same folder in a remote (WSL/SSH/dev-container) workspace fails with "already exists" instead of auto-renaming.** `resolveClipboardResources` replaces each `vscode-remote://` source with a downloaded local temp `file://` URI before it reaches the clipboard

claim: setToCopy calls resolveClipboardResources unconditionally regardless of the cut flag, so pasteFileHandler moves the temp copy and the original remote file is never deleted — cut degrades to copy.
raw: **3. Cut + paste of a remote file silently degrades to copy — the original is never deleted.** `setToCopy` calls `resolveClipboardResources` unconditionally, ignoring the `cut` flag, so the clipboard holds a local temp copy. `pasteFileHandler` then builds a move edit against that temp copy

claim: Filtering DataTransfers.TEXT to file:// scheme means dragging any vscode-remote:// resource into in-app text-capable targets (terminal, search, editors) now sets no text at all.
raw: **4. Restricting `DataTransfers.TEXT` to `file://` breaks dragging remote resources into in-app text targets.** The same TEXT channel that feeds native drops also feeds in-VS-Code text-capable areas (terminal, search, editors) — "Text: allows to paste into text-capable areas".

claim: RemoteFileSystemProxyClient.register puts registerProvider inside the onWillActivateFileSystemProvider listener, so every remote file operation after the first logs a registration failure and adds a fresh, never-disposed provider instance.
raw: **5. The proxy file-system provider re-registers on every scheme activation, logging an error and leaking a provider instance each time.** `RemoteFileSystemProxyClient.register` puts `registerProvider` *inside* the `onWillActivateFileSystemProvider` listener.

claim: resolveClipboardResources' JSDoc promises file:// URIs for all resources, but the catch block pushes the original remote-scheme URIs, contradicting the contract callers rely on.
raw: But the `catch` block at line 322 (`result.push(...remoteResources)`) pushes the original remote-scheme URIs straight into the result array when the download fails — these are not `file://` URIs at all, directly contradicting the stated contract.

claim: On a mid-loop copy failure the catch block pushes all remoteResources even though earlier successes already pushed temp targets, so the result contains both the temp copy and the original remote URI for the same file.
raw: But the `for` loop (308-316) pushes a `target` (temp local copy) into `result` for each resource as it succeeds. If the copy throws partway through (e.g. on the 3rd of 5 remote files), the `catch` block then pushes **all** of `remoteResources` (line 322)

claim: The unconditional download in setToCopy breaks cut/move semantics for remote files — the move edit is applied to the ephemeral temp copy so the original remote file is never deleted.
raw: Now `resolveClipboardResources` is called unconditionally regardless of the `cut` flag, so the clipboard ends up holding a temp `file://` copy instead. ... the "move" edit is applied to the ephemeral temp copy, not the original remote resource

claim: The comment "Uint16Array naturally uses the platform's char encoding (UTF-16)" is imprecise: the byte reinterpretation only yields UTF-16LE bytes on little-endian hosts.
raw: Minor/soft note (not flagged as a hard finding): `clipboardService.ts:230-231`'s comment "Uint16Array naturally uses the platform's char encoding (UTF-16)" glosses over endianness — the byte reinterpretation (`new Uint8Array(encoded.buffer)`) only yields UTF-16LE bytes on little-endian hosts.

claim: Restricting DataTransfers.TEXT to file:// URIs means remote workspace resources (SSH/WSL/dev-container) set no TEXT data when dragged into in-app text targets such as terminals, search, and editors.
raw: `DataTransfers.TEXT` is also consumed by in-VS-Code text targets (terminals, search, editors). Remote workspaces (SSH/WSL/dev-container) using `vscode-remote://` URIs would now have *no* TEXT data set at all when dragged to in-app text areas

claim: readResources()/hasResources() falling back sequentially across VS Code's own format and per-OS native formats reintroduces the multi-format ambiguity that PR #200601's double-paste fix removed.
raw: This PR's `readResources()`/`hasResources()` now fall back sequentially across VS Code's own format and per-OS native formats ... which reintroduces exactly the class of ambiguity #200601 fixed — multiple clipboard formats simultaneously appearing populated.

claim: A reviewer's unaddressed concern still stands: setToCopy eagerly downloads every remote resource to cacheHome, blocking the copy, and the resulting temp /tmp paths are written straight into the native clipboard.
raw: mjbvz flagged: "I feel like the temp file stuff isn't right... We are creating the file eagerly on copy and blocking the copy on this. I worry about leaking the `/tmp` file path," suggesting a `Promise<Blob>`-style clipboard API instead. mjbvz still approved the PR, but the code was not changed

claim: The new logService.trace calls log full resource paths (user data) during copy/paste — the same pattern reviewers pushed back on in PR #257428.
raw: This PR adds `logService.trace('RemoteFileSystemProxyClient#stat', resource.toString())` etc. in `src/vs/platform/files/electron-browser/remoteFileSystemProxyClient.ts` (lines ~164-174), logging full resource paths — same pattern flagged before, though at `trace` level.

claim: remoteFileSystemProxyClient.ts hard-codes PathCaseSensitive instead of deriving it from the remote OS.
raw: Copilot's comment about `remoteFileSystemProxyClient.ts` hard-coding `PathCaseSensitive` instead of deriving it from the remote OS — left unaddressed, but outside the 3 named files and lower severity since the provider is read-only.

claim: activateProvider fires the event before its provider-existence check, so the listener creates and registers a new provider on every remote file operation — registration throws, the error is swallowed, and each failed instance stays in the disposables store.
raw: 1. **Event fires unconditionally (line 99)** BEFORE the provider existence check (line 106). ... 4. **Resource leak confirmed:** Provider instances created at line 60 are added to `disposables` (line 61) BEFORE registration is attempted (line 62).

claim: Internal local-file copies now write native OS file formats to the clipboard, so both the keybinding paste and the explorerView DOM paste handler fire, causing double execution.
raw: Lines 62-104 of clipboardService.ts now write native OS file formats (NSFilenamesPboardType, text/uri-list, FileNameW) for internal local-file copies. Line 341 of explorerView.ts's DOM paste listener fires whenever `event.clipboardData?.files?.length` is non-empty

claim: writeResources writing platform-native clipboard formats on every ordinary all-local internal copy makes event.clipboardData.files non-empty on the next in-app Ctrl+V, wrongly re-triggering the native-paste path and its confirmation dialog guarded against since PR #200601.
raw: This PR's `writeResources` (clipboardService.ts:67-96) now writes to the platform-native clipboard format (`NSFilenamesPboardType`/`text/uri-list`/`FileNameW`) whenever all copied resources are local — i.e. on essentially every ordinary internal Explorer copy

claim: Narrowing setData(DataTransfers.TEXT) from all fileSystemResources to file-scheme-only nativeResources means dragging any remote/SSH/WSL/container resource into an in-VS-Code text-capable target sets no TEXT data at all.
raw: **2. `src/vs/workbench/browser/dnd.ts:238-247` — restricting `DataTransfers.TEXT` to `Schemas.file` breaks dragging remote/virtual resources into text-capable areas (terminal, search box, etc.), an explicitly documented use of this code path ("Text: allows to paste into text-capable areas").**

claim: Substituting the copied resource's URI with a local temp-download path breaks same-folder duplicate/rename-on-paste in remote workspaces, because the auto-increment check compares against the temp URI rather than the original remote URI.
raw: **3. `src/vs/workbench/contrib/files/browser/explorerService.ts:287-` (`resolveClipboardResources`) — substituting the copied resource's URI with a local temp-download path breaks same-folder duplicate/rename-on-paste for remote workspaces.**

claim: cutFileHandler sets pasteShouldMove but setToCopy unconditionally downloads remote files to temp file:// URIs, so pasteFileHandler moves the temp copies and the original remote file is left behind.
raw: `cutFileHandler` sets `pasteShouldMove=true` and calls `setToCopy(..., true)`, but `setToCopy` unconditionally calls `resolveClipboardResources`, which downloads remote files to temp `file://` URIs and writes those to the clipboard. `pasteFileHandler` then moves the temp copies

claim: If any copy in the loop throws, the catch block pushes all original remote URIs unconditionally, so files that already succeeded appear twice in the clipboard — once as a temp file:// copy and once as the original vscode-remote:// URI.
raw: **The duplication is real.** If files 1 and 2 succeed (temp URIs pushed to `result`), then file 3 fails, the result array will contain: [local files, temp1, temp2, remote1, remote2, remote3]. The same files (1 and 2) appear twice in the clipboard

claim: resolveClipboardResources downloads every remote resource to a temp file:// URI and returns that instead, breaking the source's workspace identity and causing target-exists failures on same-folder paste.
raw: The code substitution is definitively verified: `resolveClipboardResources` (lines 287–326) downloads every remote resource to a temp `file://` URI and returns that instead, breaking the source's workspace identity.

claim: On partial download failure the catch block pushes all original remote URIs including already-succeeded ones, so clipboardResources contains duplicate entries for the same logical file.
raw: If `fileService.copy()` throws partway through (e.g. the 2nd of 3 remote files fails, network hiccup, permission error), the `catch` block unconditionally does `result.push(...remoteResources)` — pushing *all* original remote URIs, including the ones that already succeeded

claim: cleanupRemoteClipboardTempDir is only called inside the remoteResources.length > 0 branch, so a subsequent purely-local copy skips cleanup and the previous temp download directory leaks on disk for the rest of the session.
raw: `cleanupRemoteClipboardTempDir()` (line 302) is only called from inside `if (remoteResources.length > 0)`. ... User later copies purely local file(s) (or nothing at all) → `remoteResources.length === 0`, so this whole block including the cleanup call is skipped.

claim: plistToFiles parses NSFilenamesPboardType with a regex over XML text, but real macOS Finder serializes that pasteboard type as a binary plist, so pasting files copied from Finder would silently return zero files (hedged, unverified).
raw: real macOS Finder typically serializes `NSFilenamesPboardType` pasteboard data as a **binary property list** (`bplist00` magic header), not XML text. If so, pasting files copied from an actual Finder window ... into VS Code would silently return zero files

claim: result is built by pushing all local resources first then all downloaded remote ones, so for a mixed local+remote multi-select copy the clipboard order no longer matches the user's Explorer selection order.
raw: `result` is built by pushing all local resources first (line 291-296), then all downloaded remote resources (line 308-316), regardless of the original selection order in `resources`. For a mixed local+remote multi-select copy, the order handed to `clipboardService.writeResources()`
